messages:
mia: quick heads-up — onboarding `mptx-24b` variant into dedicated. saw weird token drift on longer contexts, digging into RoPE scaling + MQA interactions. weights are at s3://redwood-models/mptx/2026-02-22/mptx-24b-mqa.tar.gz :eyes:

alex: thanks — can you paste the config you used for init? specifically `rope_scaling` and `group_q_attn` flags.

mia: sure, current snippet from the deploy config:
```
model: mptx-24b
rope_scaling: null
use_mqa: true
mqa_groups: auto
sliding_window: 2048
```
noticed degradation after ~2k tokens, seems like KV offsets not handled when MQA packs heads.

sanjay: hmm — if `rope_scaling` is null runtime falls back to per-layer default which assumes single-head attention. MQA needs explicit scaling factor or we get phase mismatch.

mia: got it. what value do we want? the paper suggests scale by heads_per_group ratio but our runtime expects a float per layer.

alex: suggest starting with 1.0 for all layers, then test with `rope_scaling = heads / total_heads` for grouped layers. also enable the sliding window sanity check in runtime: `--validate-kv-offsets`.

mia: running a quick smoke with `rope_scaling=0.5` and `--validate-kv-offsets` now. will post logs.

ops-bot: deploy-check started for mptx-24b on dedicated-pool-3 — build 2026-03-18_09:12:03.

kevin: small note — tokenizer has an off-by-one in EOS handling for this checkpoint (seen in tokenizers/bytepair v2). It inserts an extra padding token when `encode_plus(..., return_tensors='pt')` is used. Might explain drifting logits near sequence ends.

mia: thanks, @kevin. I ran a quick compare of decoded lengths: raw vs runtime tokenizer, confirmed +1 in ~3% of sequences. Adding a pre-tokenizer trim for now.

eva: for config validation, can we add a rule in CI that errors if `use_mqa` true and `rope_scaling` is null? That would have flagged this earlier.

alex: +1. create a small YAML schema check in model-onboard pipeline. Example rule:
```
if model.use_mqa == true and model.rope_scaling is null:
  fail('rope_scaling required when use_mqa is enabled')
```

mia: opening a PR for the CI check. pinging @sanjay for runtime fallback behavior — do we want the runtime to refuse to start or to auto-infer a safe scaling (with a warning)?

sanjay: prefer fail-fast for dedicated and private deployments (explicit config). For hosted we can auto-infer with a WARN and telemetry tag so SRE can follow up.

mia: noted. I'll make the PR set fail-fast for dedicated/private and warn for hosted.

ops-bot: logs uploaded to /var/logs/deploys/mptx-24b/1763534120/ (link: https://logs.redwood.internal/deploys/1763534120).

mia: smoke results: with `rope_scaling=0.5` and tokenizer trim, long-context drift reduced but still see occasional spikes at 3072 tokens (using sliding_window 2048, stride 1024). suspect sliding-window KV stitching bug with MQA.

kevin: can you dump KV indices from runtime when spike happens? a small snippet in runtime: `log.debug('kv_offsets', layer, kv.offsets[:8])` should help.

mia: posted a small log excerpt to the deploy logs — grep for `kv_offsets` around 00:04 in the trace.

alex: fwiw, we implemented a variant of attention where group packing changes KV layout to [B, G, L, H_per_group, Dk] vs canonical [B, L, H, Dk]. Stitching code assumes canonical layout unless `mqa_layout=true` in model meta. Are we sure the onboard meta sets that?

mia: model meta currently has `mqa_layout: auto`. maybe auto resolved wrong. I'll change to explicit `mqa_layout: true` and re-run.

sanjay: good catch. also ensure the `kv_index_map` is included in the saved weights — I've seen export scripts drop it for memory optimization.

mia: checked tarball — `kv_index_map` missing. re-exporting weights with `--include-kv-map`. will re-run deploy after upload.

eva: thanks — small ops note: please tag the PR with `onboard/mptx-24b` so we can track rollout in the console and attach canary policy.

mia: will do. final plan in thread: 1) re-export weights with kv map, 2) set `mqa_layout: true` and explicit `rope_scaling` per-layer, 3) CI check PR for rope+mqa rule, 4) re-run smoke with `--validate-kv-offsets` and attach logs.

kevin: if you want faster iteration, I can run a local harness with tiny-sharded weights to reproduce spike. ping when kv-map uploaded.

mia: thanks all — uploading new tarball now, will update when smoke completes. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-check completed: build 2026-03-18_09:18:35 — problems detected: KV map missing (previous run) — new upload queued.
